UK and France approved Kyiv's missile production, including Storm Shadow blueprints, prompting Putin to hint Russia could target UK military-industrial sites in retaliation. Russia has escalated its drone and missile war, sustaining five consecutive days of daytime air raids on Kyiv, disrupting daily life and emptying supermarket shelves; a Kyiv railway depot was hit, killing several. Strikes expanded to Odessa, hitting homes, a power plant, and a border checkpoint with Romania. Zelensky declared Russian airspace 'completely unsafe' for airlines, prompting Putin to call it 'state terrorism' and vow to respond. Ukraine is escalating its own drone campaign, striking deeper into Russia than ever and causing panic there. Drones also triggered alerts in Latvia and crossed into Estonian airspace, prompting NATO, including Turkish jets, to scramble fighters. The hybrid war has now spread to Germany: Berlin blames Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport and is investigating two new power-grid sabotage incidents, one probed as possible terrorism; Russia has summoned Germany's charge d'affaires and denied the accusations as fabricated, while the EU and NATO vow to increase pressure on Moscow.
